blocks: Table 2: This table presents items (a) through (m), which constitute the definition of a “pro-gun” bill. Through analysis of
the 2,907 bills returned in the Congress.gov search, these various clauses were determined to be relevant aspects of
legislation that seeks to expand access to firearms or ease existing restrictions on firearms. They served as the guiding
definitions for the “pro-gun” coding in this study. An example of a “pro-gun” bill is H.R. 822, which is the National
Right-to-Carry Reciprocity Act of 2011 proposed in the 112th Congress. This bill would “amend the federal criminal code
to authorize a person who is carrying a valid, government-issued identification document containing that person's
photograph and a valid permit to carry a concealed firearm in one state, and who is not prohibited from possessing,
transporting, shipping, or receiving a firearm under federal law, to possess or carry a concealed handgun (other than a
machine gun or destructive device) in another state in accordance with the restrictions of that state.” This definition fits
